source: hollywood_summary.md v6.1 (20 November 2026, 11:35 PM CST) and titles.csv in the Hollywood working files. Agreement figures from agreement_report.md v6.

agreement.note: Mike's definitional rulings applied to both coders, using the first coder's labels from before later resolutions. The current-code kappa (0.98) is partly circular because some resolutions adopted the second coder's label. The v3 figure, from before those rulings, was 93.5%, kappa 0.87 (n = 139).

definition: A slavery film has chattel slavery as a condition or institution as its organizing subject (people held as property, traded, forced labour, escaping or resisting that system). Inclusion is based on the lived experience of enslavement as the core theme. Rescue, search, adventure, romance and abolition-campaign films are excluded. Heritage of the enslavers and the enslaved is inferred from the setting when it is not named in the plot text.
definition_rulings: The Favorite (1989) is not a slavery film. Abolition-campaign films are out. Traces of the Trade and Descendant pass.

rules.fd: Financing-and-distribution rule: a US major (including specialty labels), a mini-major, a major US network or PBS, or a major streamer financed the film or handled its main US distribution. US co-productions are included.
rules.majority: Majority-partner rule: the same studio test, but a co-production counts only if the US is the majority partner. Proxy order: a published majority co-producer source (LUMIERE / European Audiovisual Observatory, AFI Catalog, BFI, treaty filings), then the nationality of the lead production company, otherwise minority/unclear and off the headline.
rules.strict: Strict US-only rule: US-only productions with a major studio, network or streamer; kept for reference.

ratios.caveat: Headline count divided by the victim baseline in millions. The baselines measure different things, so this is not a measure of fairness.

rows.subject: e
rows.note: The v6.1 ratio table listed count 1 and 0.8–1.0 per million before The Favorite (1989) was excluded. With the current headline count of 0, the ratio is 0.
